sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **16 of the official questions in Area and volume are this one** — 2 Easy, 4 Medium, 10 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question has two figures, usually squares, rectangles or triangles, described as similar or with one side 'k times' the other.
- You are given a ratio of lengths or perimeters and asked for a ratio of areas, or the other way round.
- There may be a table comparing perimeters, or a question like 'the area is n times; what is n'.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the length scale factor k.
- A ratio of perimeters equals k.
- 2) Areas scale by k², and volumes by k³.
- 3) To find a matching side, set up a proportion using k.
- To find an area, multiply the known area by k².

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Try a side length of 1: the area of the scaled figure is k², so type k^2 for the given k.
If k is large, Desmos squares it without error.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You may use k for the area instead of k².
You may also treat a perimeter ratio as an area ratio, or square it when setting up a side proportion that needs k itself.
